video_title: Wemby is the NEW VILLAIN of NBA!! Should Spurs Blow Up Their Roster?

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' collapse against the Knicks in the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: It was just wash, rinse, and repeat. It showed us the youth and the inexperience on the Spurs side.
quotes.quote: It was just wash, rinse, and repeat. It did two things to me. It showed us the youth and the inexperience on the Spurs side, and then it showed the specialness of this Knicks group and how they really were one of those teams that, if it's a boxing match, it could be ninth, tenth round, you've been getting beat up the whole time, and it's one of those fighters that you just can't sleep on because he's not going to go down and he's going to have something left. That's how the Knicks were.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Uncertainty regarding the Spurs' roster and De'Aaron Fox's future
quotes.excerpt: It is one of the trickier situations that I have seen. The financial stuff was very different.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: What do the Spurs do? Do they shake up the roster this summer? Does De'Aaron Fox's salary the next couple of seasons kind of limit what they can do?

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Amick
text_blocks.text: It is one of the trickier situations that I have seen. The reason is, on the one hand, you could look at it with glasses half full and say, the Spurs, they've been through something like this before. But the financial stuff was very different. You weren't looking at a player like De'Aaron who's on track to make $60 million and a guy like Dylan Harper who's on a rookie contract with this massive divide between these two talents. It's just not as simple as convincing De'Aaron to go to a reserve role because first of all, I don't think he's ready for that yet.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's emergence as the NBA's new villain
quotes.excerpt: He has no problem finding a highlight reel with shoving Jaylen's face all the way to the hardwood.
quotes.quote: It feels like it. Fair or not, and a lot of it's fair, you're talking about a guy who got a highlight reel. He has no problem finding a highlight reel with shoving Jaylen's face all the way to the hardwood and the elbow on Naz Reid in the previous rounds. The one thing I have been saying to people in defense of Wemby, it's a little bit like with Shaq. One of these networks should have a Wemby cam where if you want to, the camera just stays on Wemby all the time so that we can at least see all the times that he's getting hit below the belt and hitting the head. He gets beat up the whole game, and then when he reacts, he's obviously not afraid to react strongly.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown's impact on the Knicks' team culture
quotes.excerpt: A major part of their reasoning was because he had the type of personality and collaborative nature.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: You wrote that Mike Brown built a relationship with the Brunsons once he got the job. From what you have seen, what changes did Brown make behind the scenes that helped this roster get over the hump that simply Tom Thibodeau didn't do?

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Amick
text_blocks.text: The reality is that when the Knicks decided to hire Mike Brown, a major part of their reasoning was because he had the type of personality and collaborative nature that they felt like they were lacking. As close as Tom Thibodeau was with that whole group, he at times in his whole career has been known to be one of those batten down the hatches, my way or the highway type coaches. The front office, even Jim Dolan, they wanted to have their voices be heard. The players at times wanted to have their voices be heard. And so Mike represented all of that.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating Jalen Brunson's status as the greatest Knick ever
quotes.excerpt: The argument for Jalen is that this Knicks team, the help around him, outside of CAD, does not compare.
quotes.quote: I feel it's one of the rare ones where I feel like I'm not equipped because I'm young enough, which is not something I say much these days, to weigh in on Clyde, weigh in on those guys. I mean, you got two championships with loaded teams. The argument for Jalen is that this Knicks team, the help around him, outside of CAD, does not compare to what those teams in the old days had for the Knicks and so that augments Jalen's case. I mean, he's in the conversation. When his own father is saying that Patrick is the guy, maybe he's just trying to give love to his buddy, but Patrick, his case is tricky because longevity wise, impact wise, he beat everybody, but he didn't win the chip.
